## Design

### 2026-10-19 – October 19th: Idea set

**2h**

October 19th: Idea set

Instruments. Instruments are nice to listen and most like guitar and piano do one thing. Playing chords. Playing chords is essential when trying to play a piece or sing along to a song. This is why I designed Chordial.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/01a7bbb25f6bd9d968b7a25174c6de5ae101dcbc04fcce18e29e7c8ae7186274.png)

Electronics used
XIAO ESP32-C3
MAX98357A  amplifier
speaker
SSD1306 OLED
EC11 rotary encoder
 2 momentary push buttons

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/33044b92b121dfd68399054f50f687416b1ead370d97811ef48f280a9535f27c.png)
Then set up github repository. Then made the Kicad File. Ready to work tomorrow.

### 2026-10-20 – October 20th: PCB

**3h**

October 20th: PCB

Today I started my day finding all the parts that I needed and looked up how to use them in KiCAD

I decided to use the Seedstudio Xiao ESP32-S3  because it has a bit more pins than ESP32-C3.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/dd3600f5c40797e394ebf6c179c26b24f46879f741ae9263d42d4e5c6c880905.png)

Then I went researching for the audio amplifier and landed on this. And searched up how to wire them.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/7650eafca8dd79a9d37d5c2a03dec7c89d93c4c99b0695db1c9ee3ab80e96460.png)

I am definitely getting better at wiring things in KiCAD and finished the rest of all the things I needed.

![Screenshot 2026-10-20 210423](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/fd61bed5c41fef19bf442d5ad7a0bc97f10d39756aaa726b91773b88cbff5f07.png)

Basic part done. I am going to ask how to implement a battery system because I can't find a good guide online.

### 2026-10-21 – October 21st: Battery system started

**3h**

October 21st: Battery system started

Okay I first posted a help message on the halflife help channel yesterday about how to add a recharging system but no one responded. So I posted it again and luckily Dipa responded and gave me guidance.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/e57a95a0d0df300c0c4e7d4ad72375051742af6959fdf85328f29d7ec00006b1.png)

So using the frame work Dipa has given me, I looked up a similar project online that has a battery system.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/18a021e2cf7dca01bd9c8ebdb720b4730fc039e13fa2e4a6c4d51221495a5884.png)

Used both of these guidance for reference for my own project and ended up with something like this.

![Screenshot 2026-10-21 182832](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/95d6b3e95184f0135ee124cff0f37003fcfd55654446a61009f6742cd96970e1.png)

I added the USB-C adapter and MCP73871 as the charger system. Also added where the battery should charge and hopefully I can finish this complicated system tomorrow.

### 2026-10-22 – October 22nd: Massive change

**3h**

October 22nd: Massive change

So, I was continuing the complex battery system I was working on last time and I received a message from slack from someone that ESP32-S3 might have a built in battery system. So I went on the wiki for this.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/5221460031ccdeb1a96feac8369028c05ddcd8e36e5de1319e85d06f4ce4705b.png)

And read that there is a battery system and I changed my whole design to use the built in battery because I wasn't too sure if my complex battery system would work and it was adding extra work for soldering.

![Screenshot 2026-10-22 213746](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/7fb2962e2d34cff2473ba74d77809b084606a051510215f822dcb01f43ba918f.png)

I finalized the implementation and bug checked and went online and researched to put the correct footprints for each part.

![Screenshot 2026-10-22 185232](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/5e0336d8aceaf47774f564815a93aa27ac8f74b2b14b8bec66ada27193135ca3.png)

Schematic done, going to finish the pcb design tomorrow hopefully.

### 2026-10-23 – October 23th: PCB basically done.

**4h**

October 23th: PCB basically done.

Today I was sick so my work pace was drastically slow because I kept coughing.

![Screenshot 2026-10-23 214445](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/fd73a354429697b9a43d17e297c828cc4e6adc36b73492d4a9cd5b351cd7b78c.png)

First I changed the battery system so that they had pins to the actual board and I will be able to connect the battery pretty easy to the PCB using mounted soldering boards. Also I added a switch for on and off function.

Then, when I tried to add it to PCB editor, I had to add a footprint for everything and apparently the ESP32-S3 that I put using symbol editor didn't have a footprint, so I found that and added that in.

![Screenshot 2026-10-23 215932](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/d83dbb7e1e89d41edf2ea2ada6a8172572bc30389f516252eecea41eee707551.png)

Then added all the components and arranged it in a style I want (Probably going to change a bit because I want to make sure the physical part have enough space).

![Screenshot 2026-10-23 222403](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/82b8922cb3b48a56b04ab5fe18c4f04dd036be3d985ba64c508dc71704eb660c.png)

Then added the wires in and started debugging all the errors. Using DRC

![Screenshot 2026-10-23 225810](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/96c3f6daae5bb608ca2f16d5dc6715cd0f44002b716c6f04dbeff1bce791cf0a.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-23 224524](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/rsJwrjl25kbCfZE7Dltry86oScYzcoZw/8794bb4cc9ce1d1330b7b694b529c43a6fcc1a148932925b8ebfe0027c0de4e0.png)

Added everything in except the actual pcb layout. Did not decide on that yet so hopefully I get better tomorrow so I can lock in.
